title: Become a Great Engineering Manager – Course
description: A structured path through Ankita Kulkarni’s freeCodeCamp course on becoming an engineering manager. The official announcement covers the difference between an engineering manager and a technical lead, skills for career growth, communication and feedback, and what Ankita wishes she had known before the role. Written lessons are outline-only until an official transcript is available; the original YouTube video remains an optional, credited watch.

chapters.title: The Essence of Leadership (chapter times pending)

lessons.summary: The official course announcement opens on what leadership in engineering actually is: the difference between a software engineering manager and a technical lead, a roadmap toward successful leadership, and the skills needed to guide a team. Full notes will follow once a transcript is available.

quiz.question: According to the official course announcement, which contrast is part of the essence of leadership in this course?
choices: The difference between frontend and backend engineering
The difference between being a software engineering manager and a technical lead
The difference between Scrum and Kanban
The difference between junior and staff engineer titles only
quiz.explanation: The freeCodeCamp announcement lists the fundamental differences between a software engineering manager and a technical lead as a core topic in this section.

quiz.question: Besides that contrast, what else does the announcement say this leadership section covers?
choices: A roadmap to successful leadership and the skills needed to guide a team effectively
A complete Kubernetes certification syllabus
How to negotiate a vendor contract
How to write a compiler
quiz.explanation: The announcement also points to a roadmap to successful leadership and the skills necessary to guide a team effectively.

exercise.prompt: In a short paragraph, contrast the job of a software engineering manager with the job of a technical lead as you currently understand them. Note one question you want the full lesson to answer once the transcript notes are available.
exercise.hint: Stay with the announcement’s framing: what is different about the two roles, and what skills would you need to guide a team rather than only lead technically.

chapters.title: Skill Development for Career Advancement (chapter times pending)

lessons.summary: The announcement’s second area is skill development: the pivotal skills that, once mastered, can change your career trajectory and help you make a tangible impact. Detailed frameworks are pending the transcript.

quiz.question: What does the official announcement say the skill-development section is for?
choices: Learning a new programming language from scratch
Uncovering pivotal skills that, once mastered, can significantly enhance your career trajectory
Passing a system design whiteboard interview
Setting up CI/CD for a monorepo
quiz.explanation: The announcement describes this section as uncovering pivotal skills that can significantly enhance your career trajectory, especially if you want to make a tangible impact.

quiz.question: Who does freeCodeCamp say this course is aimed at?
choices: Only chief technology officers
Only people who have never written code
Individual contributors curious about engineering leadership, and current managers who want to refine their skills
Only recruiters and HR business partners
quiz.explanation: The announcement says the course is ideal for individual contributors curious about engineering leadership, as well as current managers seeking to refine their skills and strategies.

exercise.prompt: List three skills you believe would most change your career trajectory if you mastered them as a leader (or future leader). For each, write one concrete situation at work where that skill would change the outcome.
exercise.hint: The announcement frames these as pivotal skills for impact, not as a programming syllabus. Stay practical: a meeting, a promotion conversation, a project in trouble.

lessons.title: Communication and feedback in a team
lessons.summary: The announcement’s third area is the art of effective communication and feedback in a team. It stresses that a manager shapes team dynamics and performance, and that the course offers practical tips. The written playbook itself is pending the transcript.

quiz.question: What does the official announcement say you will learn in the communication and feedback section?
choices: How to write RFC documents only
The art of effective communication and feedback within a team setting
How to configure Slack notification levels
How to automate stand-up notes with a script
quiz.explanation: The announcement describes this section as learning the art of effective communication and feedback within a team setting.

quiz.question: Why does the announcement say communication and feedback matter for a manager?
choices: Because managers are measured only on lines of code they still write
Because a manager’s role in shaping the team’s dynamics and performance is crucial
Because feedback replaces the need for a product roadmap
Because communication is only needed in incident reviews
quiz.explanation: The announcement says that as a manager, your role in shaping the team’s dynamics and performance is crucial, and the course provides practical tips on how to achieve this.

exercise.prompt: Pick one recent moment with a teammate (praise, a missed deadline, or unclear work). Write the feedback you would give in four sentences: what you observed, why it mattered for the team, a question you would ask, and one request going forward.
exercise.hint: The announcement emphasizes communication and feedback as tools for team dynamics and performance, not as a one-way verdict.

lessons.title: What Ankita wishes she knew

chapters.title: Personal Growth and Reflection (chapter times pending)

lessons.summary: The announcement’s last area is personal: Ankita shares what she wishes she had known before becoming an engineering manager. It is aimed at people considering a similar transition. Her specific stories will be written up when the transcript is available.

quiz.question: What does the official announcement say Ankita shares in the personal-growth section?
choices: A list of every company she has worked at, with no reflection
Her personal experiences, including what she wishes she knew before stepping into the role of an engineering manager
A salary negotiation spreadsheet
A template resignation letter
quiz.explanation: The announcement says Ankita shares her personal experiences and offers a candid look at what she wishes she knew before becoming an engineering manager.

quiz.question: According to the announcement, what does this course emphasize beyond technical skills and project management?
choices: Only how to choose a cloud vendor
The human element in a tech environment, including empathy, communication, and team dynamics
Only how to write performance-review software
Only how to pass a coding interview
quiz.explanation: The announcement says what sets the course apart is a holistic approach: it is not just about technical skills or project management, but about the human element — empathy, communication, and team dynamics.

exercise.prompt: If you are considering (or already in) an engineering-manager role, write five things you wish you knew before the transition — or five questions you would ask someone who has made it. Keep them personal and specific to your team or company.
exercise.hint: The announcement frames this section as candid reflection before (or early in) the move into management, not as a generic tips list.
